author: reek
body: This test used to assert `vmx-enable:ok` while `vmx-enable` returned `VmxOk` unconditionally -- a test that could not fail, on a function that could not answer anything else, behind a `.skip` claiming it needed real hardware. Both halves of that are real now: the gate reads IA32_FEATURE_CONTROL, and this runs in the battery.

author: reek
body: THE EXPECTED OUTPUT IS THIS MACHINE'S, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The battery runs under codex-vm, whose firmware reports VT-x locked off, so the right answer here is `fail`. A run on a workstation with VT-x enabled in the BIOS would print `ok`, and that is not a broken test -- it is the gate doing its job on a different machine. What would be broken is `ok` HERE, because that is the old defect exactly: a machine that cannot enter VMX operation being told that it did.

author: reek
body: The reason line is printed because a refusal that does not say what to do about it sends somebody to read source. It names the MSR and its value, so the same output separates "firmware turned VT-x off" from "firmware never configured it" without a debugger.
